podcast.title: Win at Electronic Arts Festival (2000)
podcast.body: In August 2000, Jan Tempest Suni's track "Asad Jazzed Evening" was entered into an electronic arts festival in Helsinki and won. "Sunni entered the track into an electronic arts festival in Helsinki, any one."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Norwegian Programmer's Cover (2002)
podcast.body: Around Christmas 2002, a Norwegian programmer covered Jan Tempest Suni's "Asad Jazzed Evening" with permission and posted the result online. This cover later became a reference point in plagiarism accusations against Timbaland. "Then, about two years later, this would be around Christmas of 2002, a Norwegian programmer covered the song with permission and posted the result online."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Plagiarism Allegations Against Timbaland and Nelly Furtado (2006)
podcast.body: Jan Tempest Suni's "Asad Jazzed Evening" (2000) became the basis for plagiarism accusations when Nelly Furtado's song "Do It," produced by Timbaland, was released in 2006 and sounded similar. "Almost immediately, some people began to hear similarities between the song Do It and Sunni's Asad Jazzed Evening, which is when the accusations of plagiarism began to fly."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Creation of MTV Ringtones (2005)
xref.body: In January 2005, Timbaland was commissioned to create original ringtones for MTV, one of which, "Block Party," bore a resemblance to a cover of Jan Tempest Suni's "Asad Jazzed Evening." "In January 2005, Timberland gets a gig creating original ringtones for MTV."

xref.title: Plagiarism Accusations Regarding "Do It" (2006)
xref.body: Timbaland, as producer for Nelly Furtado's song "Do It" (2006), faced accusations of plagiarism due to its similarities to Jan Tempest Suni's "Asad Jazzed Evening." "Almost immediately, some people began to hear similarities between the song Do It and Sunni's Asad Jazzed Evening, which is when the accusations of plagiarism began to fly."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Plagiarism Accusations for "Do It" (2006)
xref.body: Nelly Furtado's song "Do It," released in June 2006 from her Timbaland-produced "Loose" album, immediately drew accusations of plagiarism due to its strong resemblance to Jan Tempest Suni's "Asad Jazzed Evening." "Almost immediately, some people began to hear similarities between the song Do It and Sunni's Asad Jazzed Evening, which is when the accusations of plagiarism began to fly."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Internet Outrage Over Plagiarism Allegations
xref.body: The controversy surrounding Timbaland's alleged plagiarism of Jan Tempest Suni's work led to significant "outrage" documented on YouTube, encouraging searches for "producer Timberland Rift's song from Finnish musician." "If you want to see the kind of outrage this has caused, go to YouTube and search for producer Timberland Rift's song from Finnish musician."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
